name: LeRobot
summary: LeRobot provides a standard dataset format with streaming and versioning, clean reimplementations of ACT, Diffusion Policy, pi-0, SmolVLA and others, a simulation and evaluation harness, and open hardware designs for very low-cost arms. It functions as the community's shared infrastructure layer and hosts thousands of user-contributed datasets. Version 0.6 (July 2026) widened it from a training library into a full evaluate-correct-train loop: world-model policies including VLA-JEPA, FastWAM and LingBot-VA alongside the VLAs, reward-model support, six simulation benchmarks under lerobot-eval, rollout tooling that captures human corrections, FSDP training and cloud training through HF Jobs. NVIDIA ships Isaac GR00T N1.7 and its Isaac Teleop framework into LeRobot, with the Cosmos 3 world foundation model announced as following. A companion LeRobot Humanoid reference design puts a 3D-printed bipedal platform at roughly $2,500 in parts.
innovation: A versioned, streamable dataset format that made robot data as shareable as NLP datasets.
Coupled cheap open hardware with the software stack, closing the loop for small-lab and hobbyist contribution.
From 0.6, carries world-action and world-model policy classes as first-class citizens beside VLAs, making the new architecture reproducible outside the labs that invented it.
matters: The main on-ramp into the field, and the source of the community data SmolVLA trained on.
Where a new architecture lands in LeRobot is a decent leading indicator of whether it becomes standard practice.
limits: Community data quality is highly variable, and reimplementations can drift from the original papers.
The 0.6 evaluation suites are simulation-only; real-robot comparison still needs RoboArena or RoboDojo.
lineage: Open X-Embodiment's standardization impulse turned into maintained community infrastructure.
